tools.name: search_hotels
tools.description: Finds hotels by name, destination or brand and returns each one's RoomExpert score, slug and page url. The other tools take that slug, so this is the lookup when the slug is not already known. Can rank by a single axis: "quietest rooms in Tokyo" is destination "tokyo", sort_by_axis "noise". Returns

tools.name: get_hotel
tools.description: Returns the RoomExpert verdict for one hotel: overall score, the eight axis scores and what each is based on, how deep the coverage is, the loyalty program, and the award price where a real one exists. Answers "is this hotel any good" and "what is it strong at". Returns Markdown: a score table with

tools.name: get_evidence
tools.description: Returns the cited quotes behind a hotel's scores. Each one carries the outlet that published it, what kind of document it was, and its url. Answers what a hotel is actually like: whether it is quiet, whether the beds are good, whether service holds up. Returns a Markdown list of up to `limit` quotes

tools.name: get_rates
tools.description: Returns live rooms and prices for one hotel and a stay window, with a booking link for each. It queries a metered rate supplier and is limited to 12 calls a minute per client, so it fits a traveler who has chosen a hotel rather than browsing several. Booking links are time-limited and expire within

tools.name: find_award_stays
tools.description: Lists hotels a given points balance can reach for one night, ranked by how good the redemption is against that program's own norm rather than a flat cents-per-point scale. Fits a traveler who says what they hold, e.g. "I have 300k Hyatt points". The balance is supplied by the caller and is not store
